headline: GTA VI pre-loads ignite Take-Two (+8.3%), while Microsoft slides 2.2% on Anthropic competition fears — ASX holds steady and Roosters win a classic Grand Final.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: GTA VI pre-loads went live on PS5 last night and Xbox Cloud Gaming access was confirmed for November 19. Take-Two's CEO told media that pre-sales are 'far in excess' of expectations ahead of next week's launch — investors piled in hard.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: Pilbara bounced strongly today, up 6.5% at the ASX close. No single catalyst in today's news, but the stock has been severely beaten down and analysts are watching lithium market conditions for signs of a floor. This looks like a relief rally for a deeply oversold stock.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: Emerging markets caught a bid today on the ASX, likely helped by a slight improvement in risk appetite across Asian markets. Nothing dramatic — just a solid day for the EM sleeve of the portfolio.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: The AI ETF ticked up 1.5% today as Australians continued to buy the recent AI sector dip, betting the worst of the selloff is behind us. New model releases from Anthropic and Google this week also helped sentiment.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft dropped 2.2% last night after Anthropic unveiled new tools — including enterprise document and coding features — that directly compete with Microsoft's Office and GitHub Copilot products. The market got nervous about the AI competition heating up. Microsoft is still up 20%+ overall in the portfolio, so this is a dent, not a disaster.

movers.name: BetaShares Diversified All Growth ETF
movers.note: DHHF quietly ticked up 0.5% today at the ASX close. No specific news — just a broadly steady day on the ASX, with the index up 0.27%.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: VTS edged up 0.6% at the ASX close, a slight lag to US market conditions from the prior session. The underlying US market was mixed last night, so this modest gain reflects a small positive drift.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG nudged up 0.3% today, in line with a broadly positive ASX session. Essentially flat — sitting almost exactly at cost for the portfolio.

movers.name: Alphabet (Google)
movers.note: Alphabet slipped a fraction last night (-0.4%). Post-earnings season analysis flagged that Google Cloud surged but overall profits disappointed slightly, and there's investor debate about whether its massive AI spending is paying off yet. Minor move — the long-term story is unchanged.

watch_today.title: Take-Two (TTWO): GTA VI pre-loads are live — big moment
watch_today.detail: GTA VI pre-loads opened on PS5 yesterday and Xbox Cloud Gaming access is confirmed for November 19. Take-Two's CEO says pre-sales are 'far in excess' of expectations. The stock jumped 8.3% last night to $224.64 — your position is now up ~4% overall. For a long-term holder this is exactly the catalyst you've been waiting for. Sit tight and let it play out through launch and beyond.

watch_today.title: Microsoft (MSFT): Anthropic competition spooked the market last night
watch_today.detail: MSFT fell 2.2% last night after Anthropic launched tools that rival Microsoft's Office and coding AI products. It's a real competitive threat worth watching, but Microsoft's overall AI position — via its OpenAI partnership, Azure, and GitHub Copilot — remains formidable. Your position is still up over 20% overall. No structural reason to sell — this is a 'watch the competition' moment, not a panic moment.

watch_today.title: Pilbara Minerals (PLS.AX): Big bounce today but still deeply underwater
watch_today.detail: PLS jumped 6.5% today to $3.10, which is a welcome relief — but the position is still down 54% overall (cost base ~$6.74). Today's move looks like a technical bounce on an oversold stock rather than a fundamental shift in lithium market conditions. Analysts say supply-demand dynamics for lithium remain challenging. Hold for now — the long-term lithium thesis depends on EV adoption timelines, which are still intact over a 5-10 year horizon.

watch_today.title: RBA rate hike biting: home loans falling, AUD slipping
watch_today.detail: New data shows Australian home loans are falling at a record pace following recent RBA rate hikes, and the AUD/USD has slipped to 0.6875. The AFR flags that a weaker Aussie dollar is actually making the RBA's inflation fight harder, since imported goods get more expensive. This is background noise for your portfolio — a weaker AUD does boost the AUD value of your US holdings (GOOG, MSFT, TTWO), which is a mild tailwind.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX: AI sector sentiment improving — holding steady
watch_today.detail: Your Global X AI ETF rose 1.5% today and is seeing renewed buying interest from Australians betting the AI selloff has bottomed. New model launches from Anthropic (Claude Fable 5.2) and Google (Gemini 4 Carbon) this week are keeping the sector in the headlines. Still down 16% overall, but the thesis — broad AI sector growth — is as intact as ever. Hold.

world.summary: The big global stories today are centred on the US political aftermath of midterm elections, an escalating then pausing US-Iran conflict, and ongoing Middle East instability affecting shipping lanes.

stories.title: Trump says Iran war is 'effectively over' militarily — but the region is still on edge
stories.why_it_matters: After the US and Iran exchanged strikes on islands in the Strait of Hormuz last week, Trump declared the military phase of the conflict 'effectively over' following a meeting with Qatar's Prime Minister. However, a ship was separately attacked in UAE waters this week. The Strait of Hormuz is one of the world's most critical oil shipping routes — roughly 20% of global oil passes through it. Any escalation threatens to spike oil prices, which flows through to petrol prices at the bowser for everyday Australians.

stories.title: Trump lurches further right after midterms, casts doubt on some election results
stories.why_it_matters: Despite earlier saying he would accept the midterm results, Trump has since cast doubt on some outcomes and signalled he plans to push his agenda further right following Republican setbacks. The midterms appear to have cost Republicans the House majority, with Jim Jordan elected as the new House minority leader. A divided US Congress makes big new legislation harder to pass — which markets generally treat as a neutral-to-positive for stability, though policy uncertainty remains elevated.

stories.title: Republicans elect Jim Jordan as House minority leader after midterm losses
stories.why_it_matters: Jim Jordan — one of Trump's most combative allies in Congress — has been chosen to lead House Republicans after their midterm losses. Jordan is a polarising figure known for his hardline positions and was previously a key player in multiple political investigations. His elevation signals the Republican Party is doubling down on its confrontational style rather than moderating after the election setbacks.

stories.title: F1 plans to finish the season in the Middle East despite ongoing conflict
stories.why_it_matters: Formula 1 has confirmed it intends to race out its season finale in the Middle East despite the US-Iran conflict creating security concerns in the region. The Abu Dhabi and Qatar Grands Prix are scheduled as season-ending races. This highlights how the conflict is creating ripple effects well beyond the immediate military zone — organisers, airlines, and businesses across the region are navigating elevated uncertainty.

stories.title: Ship attacked in UAE waters amid broader Middle East tensions
stories.why_it_matters: An oil tanker operator (Adnoc, the Abu Dhabi national oil company) reported one of its vessels was attacked in UAE waters this week. This is a separate incident to the US-Iran strikes and suggests broader maritime insecurity in the Gulf region. Shipping disruptions in these waters can push up global freight and oil prices — something to keep an eye on if incidents continue.

markets.summary: The ASX 200 finished the day up 0.27% to 9,153 — a quiet but positive session. Last night on Wall Street, both the S&P 500 (-0.38%) and NASDAQ (-0.74%) slipped modestly, with tech stocks under pressure from AI competition concerns. Gold hit $4,072 USD per ounce — another record — while the Aussie dollar dipped to 68.75 US cents.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Solid, quiet day on the ASX. Broad gains across most sectors.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Slipped slightly last night. Tech drag was the main culprit.

indicators.name: NASDAQ
indicators.note: Bigger fall last night — tech stocks hit by AI competition fears (Anthropic vs Microsoft).

indicators.name: Gold (USD/oz)
indicators.note: Gold keeps climbing — up another 1% last night to above $4,000. Safe-haven demand remains strong amid Middle East tensions.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Oil barely moved despite Middle East tensions easing slightly after Trump's 'effectively over' comments.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: The Aussie dollar slipped again — now sitting at 68.75 US cents. A weaker AUD boosts the value of your US holdings when converted back to dollars.

politics.summary: The Albanese government is under pressure on multiple fronts today: a landmark AI regulation package following the OpenAI Medicare hack, rising inflation fuelled by RBA rate hikes and a weaker dollar, and internal Labor tensions over Treasurer Jim Chalmers.

stories.title: Australia to introduce mandatory AI breach reporting and a new AI regulator — with possible criminal charges
stories.why_it_matters: Following a hack of Medicare data via OpenAI systems, the Albanese government is introducing world-first laws requiring AI companies to mandatorily report security incidents. It's also creating a new AI regulator and considering criminal charges for AI companies that fail to prevent harm. OpenAI itself will escape fines over the Medicare breach due to a legal loophole, but new laws aim to close that gap. This is a significant policy shift — Australia would become one of the first countries to treat AI security failures as a potential criminal matter for company executives.

stories.title: RBA rate hikes send home loans falling at record pace — but inflation is still stubborn
stories.why_it_matters: Australian home loan volumes are falling at a record rate following the RBA's rapid rate hike cycle — meaning fewer people can afford to borrow for property. But inflation is proving more persistent in Australia than in comparable countries like the US and UK, making the RBA's job harder. To make things worse, the falling Aussie dollar (now 68.75 US cents) is pushing up the cost of imports, adding more inflationary pressure. Savings account rates are rising in response to RBA hikes, so at least term deposit holders are benefiting.

stories.title: Business lobby urges Albanese to act big on economy in mid-year budget
stories.why_it_matters: Major business groups are publicly calling on the Albanese government to deliver significant economic stimulus and structural reform in the upcoming mid-year budget update (MYEFO). They're warning that without bold action, a $175 billion investment boom — particularly in energy and infrastructure — could be at risk due to regulatory and policy uncertainty. The government faces a tricky balancing act: too much stimulus could worsen inflation, but too little risks stalling growth.

stories.title: Labor internal tensions: Treasury reportedly 'silenced', pressure on Treasurer Chalmers
stories.why_it_matters: Reports are emerging of significant internal Labor tensions, with claims that Treasury has been 'silenced' on key economic advice to the government. Multiple Labor ministers have publicly called for anonymous leaking against Treasurer Jim Chalmers to stop, suggesting the conflict is real and damaging. A divided cabinet and a Treasurer under internal fire is not a great look at a time when Australia needs clear economic leadership — and markets will be watching whether Chalmers can hold his position heading into the MYEFO.

stories.title: Teal independents rush donations ahead of new political funding rules
stories.why_it_matters: The Teal independents (community-based MPs who took inner-city seats from the Liberals) are rushing to bank large donations before controversial new campaign finance laws kick in. The new rules are expected to cap or restrict how much money smaller parties and independents can receive from certain sources. If the Teals are squeezed financially, it could make it harder for them to hold their seats at the next election — which would likely benefit either the Liberals or Labor in those electorates.

ai.summary: It's a big week in AI: Anthropic has launched new Claude models that are rattling Microsoft's share price, Google released Gemini 4 Carbon, and Australia is responding to the OpenAI Medicare hack with potentially world-first criminal laws for AI companies.

stories.title: Anthropic launches Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 — claims to beat GPT-6 and Gemini 4
stories.why_it_matters: Anthropic dropped two new flagship AI models — Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 — that it claims outperform OpenAI's GPT-6 and Google's Gemini 4 Carbon on key benchmarks. Alongside the models, Anthropic released new enterprise tools for document creation and coding that go head-to-head with Microsoft Office and GitHub Copilot. That's what sent Microsoft's stock down 2.2% last night — investors are genuinely worried about the competitive threat to Microsoft's AI revenue streams.

stories.title: Google releases Gemini 4 Carbon — a new frontier model
stories.why_it_matters: Google officially launched Gemini 4 Carbon this week — its latest and most capable AI model. It's positioned as Google's answer to GPT-6 and the new Claude models. The launch is significant for GOOG holders: Google's AI strategy is very much alive and competitive, even as rivals push hard. The model is available via Google's services and API, meaning developers and businesses can start using it immediately.

stories.title: Australia to introduce world-first criminal charges for AI companies after OpenAI Medicare hack
stories.why_it_matters: Australia is drafting laws that would make it a criminal offence for AI company executives to fail to prevent serious harm caused by their systems — a world first. This follows a breach where OpenAI's systems were used to access Medicare records. A new national AI regulator will also be created to oversee the sector. OpenAI will avoid fines for the Medicare breach itself due to a gap in existing law, but new mandatory breach-reporting requirements will apply going forward. For anyone using AI tools with sensitive data (health, finance), this signals that Australia is taking AI safety seriously.

stories.title: Meta, Google, OpenAI, Anthropic all release major AI updates in one week
stories.why_it_matters: In just the past week, Meta, Google, OpenAI, and Anthropic have all released significant new AI products — from wearable AI agents to heavy-duty coding tools and new multimodal models (models that can process text, images, voice, and more at once). The pace of AI development is genuinely accelerating. For holders of GXAI.AX and GOOG, this competitive frenzy is a double-edged sword: it validates the sector's importance, but no single company is guaranteed to win.

sport.summary: The Roosters won a thrilling NRL Grand Final over the Knights 19-18, the NRL is weighing up a new Wildcard Round format, and tennis world No.1 Jannik Sinner is targeting the Australian Open after injury.

stories.title: Roosters win the 2026 NRL Grand Final 19-18 over the Knights in a thriller
stories.why_it_matters: The Sydney Roosters defeated the Newcastle Knights 19-18 at Accor Stadium in one of the tightest Grand Finals in recent memory. Just one point separated the two sides at full time. If you're a Knights fan, heartbreak — if you're a Roosters fan, celebrate. A one-point Grand Final is about as dramatic as rugby league gets.

stories.title: NRL makes shock call on Wildcard Round introduction
stories.why_it_matters: The NRL has made a surprise announcement regarding a proposed Wildcard Round — a new format that would see additional teams get a second chance at finals football. Details are still emerging, but it represents a significant structural change to the finals system that could affect which teams make the top eight and how the season is structured from 2027.

stories.title: Jannik Sinner targets Australian Open return after injury — plans December comeback
stories.why_it_matters: World No.1 Jannik Sinner has confirmed he is targeting a return to competitive tennis in December, with his sights set on January's Australian Open in Melbourne. Sinner has been sidelined with injury and is planning to play a couple of tune-up tournaments before the Open. As the top-ranked player in the world and the defending Australian Open champion, his return is a massive boost for the summer of tennis in Australia.

stories.title: Scott Selwood makes surprise code switch to Melbourne Storm
stories.why_it_matters: 169-game AFL veteran Scott Selwood has gone public about switching codes, joining the Melbourne Storm in an off-field role. Selwood, whose AFL career included stints at GWS and other clubs, says it's a 'huge honour' to join one of the NRL's most successful clubs. It's an unusual cross-code move and a bit of an unusual off-season story heading into the summer.
